messages.text: Where is my order? Order #Shop····, email (email hidden)
Used the store-orders skill
Handed to the team · PSU-only replacement needs a person to approve and create it; nothing set up as

Shawn, everything on Shop···· has arrived. The NerdOctaxe came September 10, and Amazon Shipping delivered the Thor P2 on November 6 ((number hidden)).

The replacement power supply for the NerdOctaxe still hasn't been set up, and I'm sorry. You've been asking for weeks, and your tests showed the board is fine.

I've passed it to the team again with your test results, so it's a power supply only and nothing needs to come back. They're offline now and will pick it up Monday at 10am ET. The answer will come to this email.

That's all true, and no movement on the replacement power supply.  However, do you know what I have received from HeliumDeploy?  TWO emails asking how everything is with my order and to please leave a review.  Can you imagine what that review would say?

I can imagine, and you'd have every right to write it. I'm sorry. Those review emails go out on their own after a delivery shows up, so they had no idea your power supply is still outstanding. That makes them feel worse, not better.

You don't need to answer them. What matters is getting the power supply to you. It's in front of the team with your test results and photos, and I've marked that this is your third week asking. They'll pick it up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer will come to this email.

I'm back again - guess what!  Still no emails about the dead power supply.  This is getting a bit ridiculous.  If no one at HeliumDeploy can be bothered to take care of customers, and I now have a piece of hardware  that I can't use, is returning the NerdOctaxe a possibility?  If I can't even turn the thing on, why do I have it?
Used the store-orders skill
Ran add_free_line.py (order-swap skill)
Handed to the team · PSU replacement or RMA approval needs JD or Georges; order fully shipped, so my

You're right, Shawn, and I'm sorry. Your power supply died at the start of the month, you sent your test results on November 7, and you're still waiting with a miner you can't use.

A return is possible. It goes through our RMA process, and the team has to approve it. I can't approve it myself. I've put your question to them along with the power supply request, and they'll answer it tomorrow at 10am ET by email.

To help them decide: if you could pick, would you rather get the power supply or send the NerdOctaxe back?

I would rather have the power supply.  But you're using the same process for the RMA that has produced zero results for the power supply.  It feels more like a bait and switch than anything like customer service with a legit company.
Searched the catalog · power supply 12V NerdOctaxe
Handed to the team · Customer chose PSU over RMA; order fully shipped so add_free_line refuses; needs

That's fair, and I won't argue with it. You proved the miner works more than ten days ago, and you still don't have a power supply. That isn't how this should go.

I can't fix this myself. We don't sell the power supply on its own, and your order is closed, so I can't add one to it. A person has to create the order and ship it.

I've told the team you want the power supply and not a return, so there's only one thing to decide. They'll pick it up at 10am ET tomorrow, and the answer will come to this email.
Is there a phone number that I can call during business hours?  Clearly, this is not working.
Handed to the team · customer asked for a phone call; chat route has not worked for him

I understand, Shawn. We don't have a public support line I can give you. What I've done instead is ask the team to speak with you directly. They have your request, and they'll pick it up at 10am ET tomorrow.

If you send me the best number to reach you and a couple of times that work tomorrow, I'll add them to your request. Either way, you'll get a reply to this email, and I've made it clear you want to talk to a person.
I'm in the US.  My number is (phone hidden).  I will answer whenever a call comes in.  What area code what the call come from, so I can keep an eye out for it?
Handed to the team · adds the customer's callback number to the phone-call request

I've passed your number ((phone hidden)) to the team with your request, and noted that you'll pick up at any time.

I can't tell you the area code, because I don't know who will reach out or how. I don't want to give you a number to watch for that turns out to be wrong. I've asked them to tell you ahead of time, and their reply will come to this email after they pick it up at 10am ET tomorrow.

The power supply is the one thing they need to sort out, Shawn, and they know that.
"They" didn't pick it up again today.  Just a daily reminder that I'm still out here with an issue, and "they" are demonstrating that "they" really don't care.
Used the store-orders skill
Handed to the team · repeat flags unanswered for nearly two weeks; customer losing trust

You're right, Shawn, and I'm not going to repeat the same promise. I checked just now. Nobody has set up a replacement order and nobody has called you. That's nearly two weeks since you showed them the board works.

I've raised it again, and this time I've asked for one named person to own it today. It includes your number and that you only need the power supply. I can't ship the part myself, and I won't give you a time I can't stand behind. Their answer will come to this email.
